chunks: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said:
If a man strikes with an iron weapon, then that is intentional killing.
He said: I asked him about accidental killing in which there are blood money and expiation: is it the case of a man striking another man without intending to kill him? He said: Yes.
I said: Then if he throws something and it strikes a man? He said: That is the accidental killing about which there is no doubt, and upon him are expiation and blood money.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money owed for wrongful killing
key_terms.بِالْحَدِيدَةِ: with an iron weapon or iron instrument

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith distinguish intentional killing from accidental killing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes intentional killing from accidental killing in legal terms. Striking with an iron weapon is classified as intentional, while injuring someone without intending death, or throwing something that hits a person, is treated as accidental killing requiring both kaffarah and diyyah.
